name: Azariah
overview: Azariah was a male figure in the biblical narrative, identified as the son of Jeroham and noted for his support of Joash as king of Judah. There is no record of his tribal affiliation or additional personal details beyond these facts.
namesAndTitles: The name Azariah means 'y-h-v-h has helped,' reflecting a theologically significant meaning rooted in God's assistance. This proper name is recorded in 2 Chronicles 23:1 and was not given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Azariah as the son of Jeroham, as noted in 2 Chronicles 23:1. No other family relationships are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Azariah's importance lies in his role supporting Joash's kingship in Judah, a critical moment in the kingdom's history. His identity as Jeroham's son situates him within the narrative of Judah's leadership transitions. The meaning of his name underscores the theme of divine help, fitting for one who played a part in upholding God's chosen king during a pivotal time.
